business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Symbiotec manufactures a portfolio of over 60 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs - including Hydrocortisones, Betamethasones, Methylprednisolones, Progesterones, Estrogens and Testosterones - using fermentation and multi-step complex chemical synthesis, and holds 43 US FDA DMFs and 23 EDQM CEPs as of March 31, 2026. Capabilities span three interlinked platforms: organic chemistry (flow chemistry, hydrogenation, photochemistry), biotechnology (biosynthesis, biotransformation, recombinant biologics including GLP-1 and Insulins) and forward integration into complex injectables (double-chamber vials, bags and syringes). As of March 31, 2026 it operated three complementary verticals - API products, CDMO services and complex injectables - supplying over 200 customers in over 40 countries, chiefly generic and specialty pharmaceutical companies in the United States, Europe and Asia.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Navisci Pte Ltd. — Direct Subsidiary (100% held by the Company): Singapore, company number 200700344C; wholesale of medicinal and pharmaceutical products; incorporated January 8, 2007 as Symbiotec Pharmalab (Singapore) Pte. Ltd.
- Knovea Pharmaceutical Private Limited — Direct Subsidiary (99.99%, one share held by Anil Satwani as nominee): CIN U24110MP2020PTC050978; manufacturer/loan-license manufacturer and distributor of drugs, bulk drugs and pharmaceuticals; holds the Mhow land and complex injectables facility; excluded from Adjusted ROCE as not fully commercialised; petitioner in the pending Pithampur Master Plan 2035 writ petition
- Symbiotec Zenfold Private Limited — Direct Subsidiary and Material Subsidiary (99.99%, one share held by Anil Satwani as nominee): CIN U24100MP2020PTC052495 (the RHP prints U24100MP2020PTC052496 in the Approvals section - a discrepancy a reviewer should note); chemicals, drugs, pharmaceuticals and APIs; excluded from Adjusted ROCE as not fully commercialised
- Xinjiang Symbiotec Biotechnology Limited — Direct Subsidiary (100% of registered capital): China, unified social credit code 91654000MA7ABEBB74; extraction of pharmaceutical raw materials from pregnant horse urine and related R&D, production and trading - the upstream link for the conjugated estrogen programme
- Symbiotec Biologics Private Limited — Direct Subsidiary (99.99%, one share held by Anil Satwani as nominee): CIN U21001MP2026PTC082197; incorporated February 18, 2026; biologics, biopharmaceuticals, biotherapeutics and allied pharmaceutical ingredients
- Xenamed, Corp. — Step-down Subsidiary: Delaware, USA, file number 58965328100, incorporated December 2, 2015; development, production and marketing of active pharmaceutical ingredients
- Group Companies — Nil: Affirmative nil: 'Based on the parameters set out above, our Company does not have any group companies, as on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus.' (Our Group Companies, pdf p.421). The litigation section repeats: 'Since our Company does not have any group company ... the requirement to disclose pending litigation involving the group company ... is not applicable.'
- Associates and joint ventures — Nil: Affirmative nil: 'Our Company does not have any associates or joint ventures.' (History and Certain Corporate Matters, pdf p.267)
- Rosewood Investments (advised by InvAscent) and Motilal Oswal Alternates / India Business Excellence Fund - III — Institutional shareholders with Board nomination rights under the Investment Agreement: Rosewood Investments nominates Dhananjay Mungale; India Business Excellence Fund - III nominates Rohit Mantri. The RHP also names Actis, Franklin Templeton and the late Rakesh Jhunjhunwala as past investors, and identifies the Investor Selling Shareholders in Risk Factor 31.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **API products:** Corticosteroid APIs (48 DMFs and CEPs) - Hydrocortisone, Methylprednisolone, Betamethasone, Prednisolone, Dexamethasone, Triamcinolone Acetonide, Clobetasol Propionate, Deflazacort, Steroidal-hormone APIs (18 DMFs and CEPs) - Progesterone, Testosterone, Estrogens, Androstenedione, Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate, Classical fermentation and differentiated APIs - anti-infectives, anti-fungals, immunosuppressants, enzymes, anti-parasitics; launched Mupirocin and Serratiopeptidase, Recombinant biologics - GLP-1 analogues and Insulins, Conjugated estrogens (generic Premarin) - intended to be commercialised as vaginal cream and oral tablets

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration: "Our broad capabilities are enabled by conversion of commodity plant-based derivative inputs (farm/microbe-to-pharmacy approach) and work with diverse microbial strains such as bacteria, fungi, yeast and algae to convert into high value steroid and hormonal pre-cursors. This supports backward integration and underpins our 'farm/microbe-to-pharmacy' approach. This integration allows us to make strategic, cost-effective 'make versus buy' decisions for key starting materials (KSMs) for over 80% of our products by revenue, thereby reducing external dependence for sourcing intermediates from other geographies. We are among the few backward-integrated Indian and global manufacturers capable of producing in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors, as of March 31, 2026. (Source: F&S Report)" Fermentation capabilities span four modalities: (i) biotransformation of soy-derived sterols to corticosteroid and hormone pre-cursors, with in-house control over each step from raw material to final API production; (ii) classical fermentation for pipeline APIs; (iii) recombinant protein expression technologies for GLP-1 and Insulins; and (iv) precision fermentation and synthetic biology for nutraceuticals and food applications. Forward integration: "We have strategically invested in forward integration to complement our API and fermentation strengths with capabilities in technically complex injectables. Our complex injectables platform is centered on double chamber vials (DCVs) and differentiated drug device combinations, including double chamber bags (DCBs), and double chamber syringes (DCSs). We are one of the first generics companies globally to successfully develop DCV through backward integration, by relying on in-house materials and not imports, for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate." Residual external dependence: "Our principal raw materials include phytosterols and certain fermentation-based and semi-synthetic intermediates, as KSMs for our APIs. We procure such raw materials from our suppliers based on purchase orders" and "do not enter into any long-term agreements with our suppliers." Raw material sourcing (Rs. million and % of total expenses, Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024): sourced domestically 781.35 (11.00%) / 915.79 (15.04%) / 785.62 (12.84%); raw material imports 1,868.82 (26.32%) / 1,197.36 (19.67%) / 3,275.61 (55.43%), of which United States of America 59.77 (0.84%) / 39.10 (0.64%) / 20.02 (0.34%), China 1,695.24 (23.88%) / 1,024.32 (16.82%) / 3,119.82 (52.79%), and other countries (Singapore, Malaysia and Germany) 113.81 (1.60%) / 133.94 (2.20%) / 135.76 (2.30%). "While we are in the process of increasing fermentation capacity through our commissioned Ujjain Facility to reduce our reliance on external raw materials, we continue to source some of our raw materials from third parties." Investment: "We have invested over Rs. 7,986.11 million in setting up additional capacities and capabilities in both API and complex injectables manufacturing over the last three Fiscals." Sustainability: renewable energy (solar and wind), carbon-neutral bio-briquettes, zero liquid discharge systems and re-use of treated water across all sites.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Volume of products manufactured and sold is stated as the key driver of revenue growth; capacity utilisation depends on product mix, order flow and raw material availability (Rau chemical synthesis utilisation rose to 63.49% in FY26 from 49.80% in FY25, while Pithampur chemical synthesis fell to 83.47% from 89.38% and fermentation to 72.91% from 82.52%)
- Product mix and regulated-market share drive gross margin - management attributes the rise in gross margin from 55.18% (FY24) to 60.43% (FY25) to 63.70% (FY26) to improved product mix, increasing supplies to regulated markets, operational efficiencies and controlled raw material prices
- Raw material cost intensity is falling - cost of raw materials, packing material and consumables consumed dropped to 42.55% of total expenses in FY26 from 46.89% (FY25) and 52.90% (FY24), consistent with backward integration; principal inputs are phytosterols and fermentation-based/semi-synthetic intermediates procured on purchase orders without long-term agreements, so price and availability swings are not readily passed through
- Import dependence and geographic sourcing mix - raw material imports were 26.32% of total expenses in FY26 versus 19.67% (FY25) and 55.43% (FY24), sourced from countries including China and the United States, against domestic sourcing of 11.00% (FY26)
- Customer relationships and concentration - top ten customers were 57.59% of revenue from sale of products in FY26 (55.90% FY25, 61.65% FY24); top five APIs were 62.27% of revenue from operations in FY26
- R&D spend as a margin and pipeline lever - Rs 296.95 million or 3.42% of revenue from operations in FY26, versus 4.14% in FY25 and 2.86% in FY24
- Working capital cycle and cash conversion - Operating Working Capital of Rs 2,750.50 million in FY26 (Rs 2,867.83 million FY25, Rs 2,056.58 million FY24), with net cash flow from operating activities to EBITDA swinging from 1.06x (FY24) to 0.23x (FY25) and back to 0.75x (FY26)
- Rising finance cost and leverage from the pre-IPO capex cycle - finance costs grew at an 87.09% CAGR from FY24 to FY26 to Rs 253.27 million, with net debt/EBITDA at 1.64x in FY26 after peaking at 2.51x in FY25, and depreciation and amortisation growing at a 17.15% CAGR as the new facilities capitalise
- Seasonality in the CDMO business - customers finalise annual planning leading to more invoices and higher invoice values in the fourth quarter, so quarter-on-quarter results may not be comparable
- General and Indian economic conditions are named as a significant factor affecting results of operations, alongside exchange rate exposure given 67.04% of FY26 revenue from outside India

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build on global leadership by expanding the product portfolio across steroidal-hormones in the own-API and ingredients business, entering new product categories, therapeutic areas and global markets, and capturing the shift of fermentation API production away from China
- Expand the classical fermentation API base beyond core corticosteroids - having launched Mupirocin and Serratiopeptidase - into high-value, low-volume APIs in niche therapeutic areas and speciality ingredients such as Vegan Vitamin D3 and algal-based Docosa Hexanoic Acid (DHA)
- Develop and commercialise a generic alternative to Premarin (conjugated equine estrogens) as vaginal cream and oral tablets, leveraging the farm/microbe-to-pharmacy platform and a distribution partnership with a global pharmaceutical company
- Build on fermentation capabilities and expand biotechnology offerings such as GLP-1 and Insulin, including establishing the proposed Biologics Facility in Ujjain to meet anticipated demand
- Commercialise complex injectables through differentiated drug-device combinations at the Mhow Facility, starting with the first two DCV products and extending into a 505(b)(2) pipeline plus DCBs and DCSs
- Scale up diverse CDMO offerings across the three interlinked platform technologies, using the Ujjain Facility as a base for non-pharmaceutical CDMO (precision fermentation, nutraceuticals, alternate proteins) and pursuing biologics/fermentation-API CDMO collaborations in India, the United States and Europe
- Continue investing in new technologies and R&D - reducing manufacturing costs and improving process efficiencies for existing products, and investing in automation, digitalisation and AI-driven process optimisation across laboratories and manufacturing facilities
- Partner with large companies for difficult-to-execute projects, structured around milestone payments, royalties and profit-sharing rather than one-time services, to align long-term economics and leverage partners' commercial reach and regulatory strength
- Develop differentiated APIs using synthetic biology platforms and enter complex, innovation-driven API areas including steroidal derivatives such as vitamin D2 and D3 using photochemistry capabilities

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As of March 31, 2026 the Company had two operational industrial-scale API facilities (Rau, 92 MT chemical synthesis; Pithampur SEZ, 492.67 MT chemical synthesis plus 300 KL fermentation) and had commissioned two additional facilities through Subsidiaries - a 400 KL biomanufacturing facility at Ujjain equipped with four 100 KL fermenters, and a dedicated complex injectables facility at Mhow capable of up to 20 million double chamber vials per annum. R&D and pilot-scale operations have started at both new facilities; the Mhow Facility is still in the process of applying for approvals from various regulatory bodies. Together these take aggregate maximum chemical synthesis capacity to 584.67 MT, maximum fermentation capacity to 700 KL (from 300 KL in FY25 and FY24) and complex injectables capacity to 20 million vials per annum, completing the vertically integrated 'microbe-to-pharmacy' and 'farm-to-pharmacy' platform. A further Biologics Facility at Ujjain is under construction and yet to be commissioned: the RHP describes it as a proposed dedicated 14 KL fermentation capacity comprising two reactors of 7 KL each, intended to cater to increasing demand for GLP-1 and Insulin. The Ujjain Facility has additional space designed in for further fermenters and the Mhow Facility has space for further expansion. The Company states it invested over Rs 7,986.11 million in additional capacities and capabilities across API and complex injectables manufacturing over the last three Fiscals, including Rs 4,794.58 million in the Ujjain Facility and Rs 3,919.19 million in the Mhow Facility as of March 31, 2026. Notably, none of the Fresh Issue proceeds fund this expansion - the Objects of the Offer are limited to debt repayment and general corporate purposes, so the capex has been funded from internal accruals and borrowings ahead of listing.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global leadership in corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs - 38.2% global volume share in corticosteroid and 23.8% in steroidal-hormone APIs in Fiscal 2026 (excluding androstenedione and hydroxyprogesterone caproate), and the only Indian and global company present across the top 10 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs (per F&S Report, commissioned and paid for by the Company)
- Molecule-level dominance in Hydrocortisone (80.1%), Testosterone (76.4%) and Methylprednisolone (76.0%) volume market share in Fiscal 2026, with a portfolio of over 60 APIs covering 90% of corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone API products (per F&S Report)
- Backward-integrated 'farm/microbe-to-pharmacy' platform - in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors from soy-derived sterols allow cost-effective make-versus-buy decisions on key starting materials for over 80% of products by revenue, reducing dependence on imported intermediates
- Multi-scale fermentation flexibility - fermenters of 5 KL, 35 KL and 100 KL spanning low-volume/high-value to high-volume products, described as one of India's largest industrial-scale fermentation capacities at 700 KL following commissioning of the Ujjain and Mhow Facilities
- Clean regulatory track record across US FDA, EU-GMP, WHO-GMP, PMDA and ANVISA - no critical observations from global regulators over the last three Fiscals, with long-standing accreditations (US FDA for 16 years at Rau, 13 years at Pithampur)
- Sticky, long-vintage customer base - over 200 customers in over 40 countries, average relationship tenure of more than ten years with the top five and top ten customers, two of the top five being innovators; high switching costs from product-specific validation, bioequivalence studies and DMF/CEP filings
- Differentiated chemistry - APIs and products with up to 400 synthesis steps validated under cGMP, and a conjugated estrogen API with 82 US FDA mandated components, one of the few globally to have developed it
- First-mover in generic double chamber vials - among the first generics companies globally to develop DCVs through backward integration using in-house materials for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate
- Expanding gross margin and high adjusted capital efficiency - gross margin 63.70% in FY26 versus 55.18% in FY24; adjusted ROCE (excluding not-yet-commercialised subsidiaries) 30.43% in FY26 versus 24.59% in FY24; CARE A+ rating in each of the three preceding Fiscals
- Sustainability infrastructure - continuous flow chemistry for Progesterone, renewable energy (solar and wind), carbon-neutral bio-briquettes, zero liquid discharge and treated-water reuse across all sites

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Extreme product and portfolio concentration in APIs — Sale of APIs was 96.07%, 99.10% and 100.00% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the top five APIs alone were 62.27%, 63.16% and 60.37%. The two newer verticals contributed only 3.80% (complex injectables) and 0.13% (CDMO) in FY26, so any demand fall or production disruption in a handful of steroid molecules hits nearly all revenue.
- Customer concentration with a small, long-tenured base — Top ten customers were 57.59%, 55.90% and 61.65% of revenue from sale of products in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and top five were 43.01%, 42.27% and 48.51%. Two of the top five are innovators. The same switching costs that create stickiness make any single loss slow and expensive to replace.
- Regulatory approval and inspection dependence across multiple jurisdictions — Facilities are subject to periodic inspections by the US FDA, EU-GMP, WHO-GMP, PMDA, ANVISA and Korean MFDS, and access to regulated markets rests on 43 DMFs and 23 CEPs. The Mhow Facility is still applying for approvals from various regulatory bodies. An adverse observation or import alert would close off the highest-margin regulated markets.
- Heavy pre-listing capex now awaiting commercialisation and utilisation — Over Rs 7,986.11 million was invested over three Fiscals, including Rs 4,794.58 million in the Ujjain Facility and Rs 3,919.19 million in the Mhow Facility, both of which are only at R&D and pilot scale. Depreciation grew at a 17.15% CAGR and finance costs at 87.09%, while the Objects of the Offer fund no expansion. Risk Factor 37 flags under-utilisation directly, and Knovea and Symbiotec Zenfold are excluded from Adjusted ROCE precisely because they are not fully commercialised - which is why reported ROCE fell to 11.56% while adjusted ROCE rose to 30.43%.
- Working capital intensity and volatile cash conversion — Operating Working Capital was Rs 2,750.50 million in FY26 against Rs 2,056.58 million in FY24 (15.65% CAGR), and net cash flow from operating activities to EBITDA swung from 1.06x (FY24) to 0.23x (FY25) to 0.75x (FY26). Total current liabilities of Rs 5,275.65 million exceeded total current assets of Rs 4,855.44 million as of March 31, 2026.
- Raw material sourcing dependence, including on China, without long-term supply agreements — Raw materials are procured on purchase orders only. Purchases from the top ten suppliers were 25.50%, 18.41% and 50.33% of total expenses in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and raw material imports were 26.32% of total expenses in FY26 (55.43% in FY24), sourced from countries including China and the United States. Phytosterols in particular are imported.
- Single-state geographic concentration of all manufacturing and R&D — Both operational API facilities (Rau, Pithampur SEZ), both newly commissioned facilities (Ujjain, Mhow), the proposed Biologics Facility and all three R&D centres are in Madhya Pradesh. Certain facilities are on leasehold rather than owned land, and the Mhow land is itself the subject of a pending writ petition over the Draft Pithampur Master Plan 2035 reclassifying it as residential.
- Unproven new verticals and an unbuilt biologics facility carrying the growth narrative — Risk Factor 22 warns the Company may not be successful in commercialising complex injectables, and Risk Factor 25 warns the Biologics Facility may face delays, cost overruns or fail to commercialise at all. CDMO began only in Fiscal 2025 and its revenue fell from Rs 68.00 million (FY25) to Rs 10.94 million (FY26). Several CDMO commitments are take-or-pay contracts and term sheets with unnamed counterparties.
- Market-share and industry claims rest on a commissioned report — The leadership statistics (38.2%, 23.8%, 80.1%, 76.4%, 76.0%, 90% portfolio coverage) all derive from the F&S Report by Frost & Sullivan (India) Private Limited, exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company for the Offer, a limitation the RHP itself flags at Risk Factor 55. Risk Factor 39 separately warns the over-50% volume shares may not be sustainable.
